title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: guess: High-purity elemental powders Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, and Ti (nominally equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi) as the feedstock for a high-entropy alloy, blended with a process control agent and loaded for high-energy milling.
recollection.intervention: guess: High-energy mechanical alloying to produce a nanocrystalline/metastable solid-solution powder, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at roughly 900–1100°C for a short dwell (minutes) under ~40–60 MPa. The SPS temperature/time were varied to extract growth/densification kinetics (Arrhenius analysis).
recollection.structure: guess: After MA: predominantly a single-phase FCC nanocrystalline solid solution. After SPS: a dense (>98%) dual-phase or multiphase microstructure comprised of an FCC matrix with a Ti/Cr-rich Laves intermetallic (C14/C15) dispersed; in some conditions, a minor BCC-like phase may also appear. Nanoscale grains retained due to rapid SPS.
recollection.mechanism: guess: Ti partitions during SPS and drives formation of hard Laves intermetallic from the supersaturated FCC solid solution. Sluggish diffusion plus short SPS dwell suppresses grain growth. Hardness arises from combined solid-solution strengthening and dispersion/precipitation strengthening (load-bearing and Orowan mechanisms) by the Laves phase; rapid Joule heating and pressure aid densification while limiting coarsening.
recollection.results: guess: Near-full density compacts with ultrahigh hardness relative to CoCrFeNi baseline, on the order of ~12–16 GPa nanoindentation hardness (≈1200–1600 HV). XRD/SEM-EDS indicate FCC + Laves dual-phase with Ti/Cr enrichment in Laves and Ni/Co/Fe enrichment in FCC. Crystallite size grows from ~10–20 nm post-MA to ~30–60 nm after SPS. An Arrhenius-type analysis yields an effective activation energy for grain/crystallite growth in the ~180–250 kJ/mol range with a growth exponent near ~2; densification surpasses ~98% theoretical.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies high-energy mechanical alloying followed by short-dwell SPS and gives a reasonably close temperature range. It also correctly anticipates retained nanoscale grains, but incorrectly makes a Ti/Cr-rich Laves phase central; the reported structure was 83% FCC and 17% BCC. The strengthening explanation includes valid solid-solution and grain-growth-suppression ideas but misses the reported Hall–Petch/dislocation-density mechanism and relies on an unsupported Laves precipitation mechanism. The estimated hardness (1200–1600 HV) is far above the actual 675 HV, and the actual compressive strength (1894 MPa) and yield stress (1238 MPa) are not recalled.
